purpose: derive the bank service operations from the integration material

notes: The IVR integration document (BRIEF section 6) was not in the material I was given, so I could not use its paths. Following the fallback rule, every operation uses POST and the service name with dots turned into slashes (cards.list -> /cards/list, and so on), with a JSON body. If the integration document defines other paths, methods, headers or request fields, use those instead.

Request field names come from the test data: customerNo (the customer key in test-customers.json), cardNumber (services called with a card are keyed by the masked number from cards.list) and newStatementWeek (the second key of statement.week.decide and statement.week.change). customerNo is filled from the call variable customerNumber.
Test data marks statement.pdf.send and contact.email.get per customer, not per card, so they only take customerNo. The flow drawing does not say which card's statement is sent.
cards.balance returns the card masked differently ("5400********1234") from cards.list ("540000******1234"). Always send the cards.list value as cardNumber.
statementWeek and statementDay are integers in statement.week.get and statement.week.decide but strings ("2", "9") in statement.week.change. They are kept exactly as written.

I saw only the first part of test-customers.json (customer 90000001 and the start of 92030487). So only 200 success bodies are listed here. Any error responses, other HTTP statuses or delays (gecikmeSaniye) that the full file has for other customers are not listed, and must be taken from the full test data, not invented. The description calls the body 'yanit', but the data uses the key 'response'; I followed the data.
No fixed auth headers or channel codes appear in the material I was given, so auth_headers is empty and no fixed params are set.
